# NavStack

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:nav-stack` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A controlled one-pane navigation stack that keeps prior views mounted, slides content on push and pop, cross-fades per-view chrome, and moves/restores focus.

## When to use

Present a single linear or drill-down flow while preserving each prior view's state, scroll position, and place in the stack.

- A compact surface shows one view at a time and navigation pushes into details or pops back.
- A simple single-pane screen needs the same stable app-layout contract without any nested navigation.

**Not when:**

- Do not use NavStack when a list and detail should remain visible together; use SplitView.
- Do not use it for co-equal top-level destinations on compact devices; wrap one stack per destination in TabNavigator.

**Alternatives:**

- [SplitView](./split-view.md) (roomy-alternative) — Promote a list-to-detail stack to SplitView once both regions fit together.
- [TabNavigator](./tab-navigator.md) (composes-with) — Use one NavStack as each TabNavigator tab's persistent content.
- [ContentSwap](./content-swap.md) (nearest) — Use ContentSwap to swap content in place inside one region without navigation chrome.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/nav-stack` — exports `NavStackView`, `NavStackToolbarConfig`, `NavStackProps`, `NavStackChromePresentation`, `NavStackBottomToolbarPresentation`, `NavStack`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/nav-stack` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/nav-stack.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Wiring: `wireNavStack` from `@kerfjs/ui/wire-nav-stack` (required).
- Wiring: `wireScrollDividers` from `@kerfjs/ui/wire-scroll-dividers` (optional).
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/nav-stack`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuinav-stack), [`@kerfjs/ui/wire-nav-stack`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuiwire-nav-stack), [`@kerfjs/ui/wire-scroll-dividers`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuiwire-scroll-dividers) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- single root view
- pushed detail view
- toolbar hidden
- configured top toolbar
- custom back icon or visible back text
- per-view bottom toolbar
- persistent final top-toolbar group (panelToggle) when embedded in a Workbench panel
- persistent bottom-toolbar fallback
- chrome and bottom-toolbar dividers only while the active view scrolls beneath them (wired by wireScrollDividers)
- permanent or no chrome dividers (chromeDividers always or none)
- translucent top chrome laid over the active view (chromePresentation overlay, measured by wireNavStack)
- translucent bottom toolbar laid over the active view (bottomToolbarPresentation overlay, measured by wireNavStack)
- app-chosen stack background color (background); overlay chrome keeps the chrome material

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [Toolbar](./toolbar.md), [ToolbarControlGroup](./toolbar-control-group.md), [ToolbarText](./toolbar-text.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** ordered view stack and stable keys; view content and structured top and bottom toolbar configurations; push and pop actions; preferred initial focus targets when DOM order is insufficient; per-view bottom toolbar or a persistent structured fallback; per-view leading, center, and trailing top-toolbar groups; per-view header and footer with List and Pane configuration; top-toolbar defaults, title size, and heading level; whether the chrome and bottom-toolbar dividers follow the scroll, always show, or never show (chromeDividers); whether the top chrome docks above the active view or lies over it on the translucent chrome material (chromePresentation); whether the bottom toolbar docks below the active view or lies over it on the translucent chrome material (bottomToolbarPresentation); an optional app-chosen color for the stack, its docked chrome and bottom toolbar, and every view (background, a typed CssColor); one view's own color goes in its pane: { background }.

**Wiring:** `wireNavStack`, `wireScrollDividers` is required.

- Use wireNavStack as documented.

**Wiring-owned state attributes** — never render, remove, or branch on these as app state:

- `data-nav-chrome-transition` on `kui-nav-stack` (`wireNavStack`): "true" while the chrome cross-fades between the outgoing and incoming view.
- `data-nav-chrome-copy` on `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy` (`wireNavStack`): Marks the inert, aria-hidden snapshot of the outgoing chrome shown during the cross-fade.
- `data-nav-revealed` on `kui-nav-stack__view` (`wireNavStack`): "true" on the preserved, aria-hidden previous view while an incoming view slides over it.
- `data-nav-exiting` on `kui-nav-stack__view` (`wireNavStack`): "true" on a popped view the helper briefly re-inserts to slide it out.
- `data-chrome-overlay` on `kui-nav-stack` (`wireNavStack`): measured once the helper has measured an overlay chrome (chromePresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height on the stack root; the chrome then lies over the active view, which clears it through the block-start edge context. Both are re-applied if a re-render drops them.
- `data-bottom-toolbar-overlay` on `kui-nav-stack` (`wireNavStack`): measured once the helper has measured an overlay bottom toolbar (bottomToolbarPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height on the stack root; the toolbar then lies over the active view, which clears it through the block-end edge context. Both are re-applied if a re-render drops them.
- `data-scroll-overflow` on `the active kui-nav-stack__view, or the kui-pane__content of a sole Pane in it` (`wireScrollDividers`): The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.
- `data-scroll-divider` on `kui-nav-stack__chrome and kui-nav-stack__bottom` (`wireScrollDividers`): The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.
- `data-header-overlay` on `kui-pane` (`wireScrollDividers`): measured once the wiring has measured a Pane's overlay header (headerPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height as --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start on the Pane root, plus a classic content scrollbar's inline size as --kui-pane-scrollbar-inline-size, which the header leaves uncovered. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: conditional · padding: child (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- The stack owns its full-height chrome and viewport; each view owns its internal content padding and scrollable content.
- The top chrome's bottom line and the bottom toolbar's top line are scroll state (wireScrollDividers), drawn as an overlaid 1px pseudo-element on the chrome and the bottom toolbar's always-present 1px top border, so neither moves the chrome or the content.
- chromePresentation overlay: once wireNavStack measures the live chrome (never a cross-fading copy), the chrome lies over the viewport's top edge and its border-box height, top safe area included, becomes the viewport's block-start --kui-edge-inset-\* context, so a plain view, a sole Pane, or a nested layout pads and scroll-pads by it automatically; the chrome ends where a classic scrollbar in the active view begins, so its track stays uncovered; unwired, or with hideToolbar, the chrome stays docked.
- bottomToolbarPresentation overlay: once wireNavStack measures the live bottom toolbar (never a cross-fading copy), the toolbar lies over the viewport's bottom edge and its border-box height, bottom safe area and divider border included, becomes the viewport's block-end --kui-edge-inset-\* context, so a plain view, a sole Pane (its content, or its footer), or a nested layout pads and scroll-pads by it automatically and the last item rests just above the toolbar; it ends where a classic scrollbar in the active view begins; unwired, or while no bottom toolbar is shown, it stays docked. It is independent of chromePresentation, which governs only the top chrome.

## Accessibility

- Give the stack region an accessible label and every back control a stable action label; visible backText names the control itself.
- Set toolbarConfig.headingLevel when the view title is the page's or section's heading landmark.
- Use wireNavStack so each controlled push moves focus into the new top view and each pop restores the revealed view's remembered descendant.
- Mark a preferred initial heading or control with data-nav-focus when the first enabled focusable descendant is not the right target.
- Overlay chrome (chromePresentation overlay) keeps WCAG AA over content passing beneath the translucent material: an untoned ToolbarText there takes the normal text color for its title and lifts its description halfway toward it; keep other quiet copy in the view. The material turns opaque under reduced transparency, increased contrast, forced colors, or without backdrop-filter.
- An overlay bottom toolbar (bottomToolbarPresentation overlay) keeps the same AA rule: an untoned ToolbarText there lifts its title and description, and a default-tone ToolbarControlGroup in either overlaid bar takes the normal text color for its controls. Its 1px top edge stays visible in forced colors.
- A background color is app-chosen: Keep text at WCAG AA over the color: a dark background needs dark-tone content or a scoped tint; forced colors paint Canvas instead.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-nav-stack`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome`, `kui-nav-stack__bottom`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome--entering`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy--bottom`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy--exiting`, `kui-nav-stack__viewport`, `kui-nav-stack__view`, `kui-nav-stack__view--entering`, `kui-nav-stack__view--exiting`.

Never put `kui-nav-stack`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome`, `kui-nav-stack__bottom`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome--entering`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy--bottom`, `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy--exiting`, `kui-nav-stack__viewport`, `kui-nav-stack__view`, `kui-nav-stack__view--entering`, `kui-nav-stack__view--exiting` on an element you write; render `NavStack` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Public tokens it reads: `--kui-nav-stack-transition-duration`. Set a token only where its public contract allows; prefer a prop.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
